title: Dynamic pixel-binning mode and ARIA-aware annotation interactions for dense time series
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Introduce a new ‘dynamic pixel-binning’ render mode and ARIA-aware annotation/tooltip behaviors for our high-density time-series chart component. Goals: 1) reduce rendering cost and mouse event churn for charts with >10k points without losing meaningful signal; 2) preserve keyboard and screen-reader discoverability for annotations, tooltips and legend interactions; 3) align color and spacing tokens with Design System v3; 4) provide a safe runtime fallback for low-power devices.
acceptance_criteria: New 'pixel-binning' render mode available as chart prop (mode: 'adaptive' | 'pixel-bin' | 'point')
Charts with pixel-bin enabled render 3x fewer canvas draw calls on example datasets (10k+ points) compared to point mode
Hover and click interactions still surface exact datapoint values for the visible time window via a sampled index; tooltips read out via aria-live when focused
Keyboard navigation: tab focuses legend items and annotations; arrow keys move annotation focus left/right through visible points
Design tokens used: chart-line-width, chart-annotation-gap, chart-legend-collapse-threshold documented in token spec
When reduced-motion or prefers-reduced-data is set, component defaults to pixel-bin with simplified tooltips
Unit tests and visual regression snapshots added; perf benchmark dashboard link included in ticket
design_decisions: Pixel-binning algorithm: group points by pixel column on the x-axis, compute min/max/avg per bin and draw a vertical micro-area to preserve envelope
Sampling policy: always keep first/last and any outliers beyond 2*stddev within a bin to avoid losing spikes
Interaction model: hover shows an interpolated tooltip representing nearest-sampled point; clicking opens full-detail drawer with exact values fetched from server if dataset is remote
Accessibility: tooltips exposed via aria-live region and aria-describedby on chart svg container; annotations have role='button' for keyboard focusability
Legend behavior: items are toggleable and keyboard operable; when many series exist (>12) legend switches to an overflow menu with checklists
Fallbacks: fallback to offscreen-canvas rasterization for older browsers; when GPU timers indicate frame budget exceeded, automatically reduce pixel-bin resolution
Tokens: reuse color tokens from palette/chart-quantity and introduce semantic tokens for 'trend-positive' / 'trend-negative'
tradeoffs_and_risks: Binning reduces visual fidelity for sparse but important transient events; mitigated by keeping outliers in bins and offering a 'zoom-to-raw' action
ARIA live verbosity vs noise: too-chatty live announcements can overwhelm screen reader users; default to concise summaries with an opt-in verbose mode
Increased complexity in runtime selection logic may require more observability knobs and new metrics; added to ENG-4012
Legend overflow interactions may be unfamiliar to users who expect full inline legend; will include micro-copy and a short tour
